subject: DPA: retention triggering events and rollback plan
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@edgeapps.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
Cc: EdgeApps, Inc. Legal <legal@edgeapps.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on retention triggers and rollback plan for DPA redline

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for walking us through the platform yesterday. Our legal team is working through the DPA redlines and we have a couple of open questions that matter for our compliance sign-off:

1) Triggering events for retention: the draft says data is retained until "business need expires" or "legal hold" — can you clarify what concrete events cause retention to extend (e.g., open support case, troubleshooting snapshot request, active billing dispute)? We need a non-ambiguous list or an operational playbook reference.

2) Rollback / restoration plan after a retention-sunset: if we request erasure and later discover we need an item for fraud investigation within the 90-day window, what's the recovery window and are backups considered before or after deletion? In other words, what is the sequence and who owns the timeline for rollback?

3) Onshore handover for deletion evidence: for EU-data-subject erasure requests, your team previously mentioned an "onshore handover" option. Can you confirm the format of proof (signed manifest, timestamps, hashes) and the expected SLA for providing that evidence to us or regulators?

We attached our redline (EdgeApps_DPA_Redlines_v2.docx) with suggested tweaks — mostly around enumerating triggering events and adding a short rollback appendix. Would appreciate a short written response with sample language, and if needed we can set a 30-minute call.

Best,
Maria

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear notes and the redline. Quick answers below, plus attached our operational playbook excerpt (redwood_erase_playbook_v1.pdf) that spells out events and evidence types.

1) Retention-triggering events (proposed observable list):
  - Open support ticket flagged for data retention or debugging (ticket ID required)
  - Active billing dispute tied to specific records (invoice/dispute ID)
  - Lawful process / investigation request from competent authority (process ID)
  - Customer-requested temporary hold (explicit documented request)
  - Export snapshot for migration requested by customer (snapshot ID)

If none of the above apply, data moves to the scheduled erasure pipeline after the agreed TTL. We can insert these items as enumerated exceptions in the DPA appendix.

2) Rollback / restoration:
  - If erasure is executed, we retain a 14-day soft-window where a rollback may be possible for operationally requested restores (human-reviewed). After 14 days, deletion is irreversible for primary copies; backups used for disaster recovery are rotated per our backup retention schedule and are not considered a reliable restoration source for erased customer data.
  - We propose DPA language: "Customer-initiated erasures include a 14-calendar-day reversible window during which Redwood may, at Customer's documented request, perform a targeted restoration. After this window, erasure is irreversible and backups will be considered expunged per the backup retention schedule."

3) Onshore handover / proof of erasure:
  - Evidence package: signed manifest (operator ID and timestamp), deletion run log (job id, affected keys), and SHA256 hashes of pre- and post-erasure manifests where applicable.
  - SLA: we can commit to providing the full evidence package within 10 business days of request for EU-residency accounts under the Private deployment or Dedicated SLA. For Hosted accounts, standard response is 15 business days.

I've looped in Laura from Legal to convert the above into DPA wording and to confirm the recovery window language. If that looks acceptable, we can mark the redline and prep a short call.

Best,

Hi all,

Thanks Ben — I drafted proposed DPA clauses below based on the operational summary. Maria, these are intentionally prescriptive to avoid ambiguous "business need" phrasing. Please let us know any substantive conflicts.

Proposed additions to DPA (Retention Exceptions clause):
  "Retention may be extended beyond the standard retention TTL only if one or more of the following documented events occur: (i) an open Support Ticket with a documented retention request and ticket identifier; (ii) a documented Billing Dispute tied to Customer data; (iii) a lawful request or legal hold issued by a competent authority; (iv) a documented Customer request to temporarily hold specified records; (v) a Customer-requested export/migration snapshot."

Proposed Rollback (Erase Reversal clause):
  "Customer-initiated erasure requests will be executed within the agreed SLA. Upon execution, Customer has a 14-calendar-day reversible window during which Redwood may, upon documented Customer request, attempt a targeted restoration from operational copies. Reversal is subject to verification and may require Customer-provided justification. After the 14-calendar-day reversible window, the erasure will be considered final and irreversible. Backups retained for disaster recovery will be rotated in accordance with the backup retention policy and are not a guaranteed source for post-erasure restoration."

Proof of Erasure (Evidence clause):
  "Upon Customer request, Redwood will provide a Proof of Erasure package consisting of: (a) operator-signed deletion manifest with timestamps; (b) execution logs indicating job ids and affected object ids; (c) cryptographic checksums of pre- and post-deletion manifests where available. For accounts with EU residency or under Dedicated/Private deployment, Redwood will provide the evidence package within 10 business days; for Hosted accounts, within 15 business days."

Clarifications / open items for EdgeApps:
  - Do you require the reversible window to be extended beyond 14 days (we can offer 30 days for Dedicated contracts with pricing impact)?
  - For exports/migration snapshots: do you want these treated as separate copy class (i.e., customer-owned snapshot) exempt from erasure?

If Maria confirms the above and whether they need the 30-day option, we can incorporate the clauses as a new Appendix A and ship a redline back to you.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Laura — thanks, that reads very clear. A few quick responses:

- The enumerated triggering events look good and match what we expected.
- We do not need the 30-day reversible window for this contract; 14 days is acceptable.
- For migration snapshots: wed like them classified as "customer-owned exports" and therefore excluded from the standard erasure pipeline, provided the snapshot is requested by EdgeApps and stored under the customer's control or explicit export manifest.

Next steps: if you can push the Appendix A text into the redline and send back a marked-up DPA, we will review and aim to close legal comments this week. Also happy to do a 20-minute call if you prefer to finalize language live.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Best,
Maria Gomez
